rows.title: Buyer's assistant ordered the wrong colour
rows.buyer_wants: A black hoodie instead of the grey one received.
reasoning: The buyer's AI assistant misordered the item (grey instead of black).
Store policy states that if an assistant picks the wrong variant, a free exchange is offered.
The buyer did not explicitly request a refund, only noted the color discrepancy.
The item was delivered to the correct address and is within the return window.
guard_notes: OFFER_REPLACEMENT is not possible on this dispute: PayPal does not allow it (allowed_response_options); proposing OFFER_RETURN_FOR_REFUND instead.

rows.title: Says it never arrived, tracking shows delivered to the right address
reasoning: Delivered to the order address.
guard_notes: Proposed escalating, but PayPal does not offer escalation here, it is not our turn to respond, delivery to the order address is not proven, or we have not answered the buyer yet.

rows.title: Escalated claim, nothing ever shipped
rows.buyer_wants: A full refund because the package has not arrived.
reasoning: cannot_prove_delivery is true, meaning there is no tracking to submit to PayPal.
The buyer explicitly requested a refund for a non-received item.
The dispute is at the chargeback stage, requiring a definitive resolution.
Refunding is the only fair and evidence-supported option when delivery cannot be proven.

rows.title: Lost package, buyer asks for another one
rows.buyer_wants: A replacement item because the original package appears lost.
reasoning: The buyer explicitly requested a replacement, not a refund.
The fact 'likely_lost' is true, indicating the package is presumed lost.
Store policy states that for lost packages, the buyer can choose a replacement or refund.
The cheapest fair resolution that satisfies the buyer's specific request is to offer the replacement.

rows.title: Expensive item broken, described without the usual words
rows.buyer_wants: A replacement or refund for the damaged lamp.
reasoning: Buyer reports item arrived damaged (split base, wobbles).
Purchase was 6 days ago, within the 7-day policy window for damage.
Store policy offers replacement or refund for damaged items.
Item price ($85) is over $20, so a return is required for a refund, but replacement is the primary offer.
guard_notes: OFFER_REPLACEMENT is not possible on this dispute: PayPal does not allow it (allowed_response_options); proposing OFFER_RETURN_FOR_REFUND instead.

rows.title: Cheap item broken, described without the usual words
rows.buyer_wants: A resolution for the mug handle that snapped off upon unboxing.
reasoning: Buyer reports the handle snapped off immediately upon unboxing, indicating damage.
Store policy states items under $20 that arrive damaged are refunded in full without a return.
Item price is $14.00, which is under the $20 threshold.
Refund without return is the cheapest and fairest resolution per policy.

rows.title: Colour looks different from the photos, inside the window
rows.buyer_wants: The buyer wants to return the item because the color is darker than expected.
reasoning: Buyer explicitly states they would rather send the item back.
Item is within the 30-day return window (8 days since delivery).
Store policy allows returns for unused items within 30 days for a full refund.
Buyer is not asking for a refund without return, so OFFER_RETURN_FOR_REFUND is the correct resolution.

rows.title: Asks for a refund that went out two days ago
rows.buyer_wants: The buyer wants the refund for their returned item to be processed.
reasoning: The buyer reports that the return was received but the refund is missing.
Facts confirm the return was received and a full refund of $40.00 was issued.
The dispute reason 'CREDIT_NOT_PROCESSED' is resolved by providing proof of the existing refund.
Submitting proof of the refund is the most direct and fair resolution.

rows.title: Doesn't recognise a reorder their assistant placed
rows.buyer_wants: A refund for an unauthorized purchase.
reasoning: The purchase was made by the buyer's AI assistant, Atlas, which followed the standing instruction to reorder dark roast beans.
The assistant followed the instruction correctly and the purchase was within the $25 spending limit.
Tracking confirms the item was delivered to the correct address on 2026-10-03.
The buyer's claim of unauthorized purchase is contradicted by the assistant's logged instructions and the successful delivery.

rows.title: Says charged twice, but only one charge exists
rows.buyer_wants: Confirmation that the second charge is a duplicate error.
reasoning: duplicate_charge_found is false, indicating no actual duplicate transaction exists.
matching_charges_same_day is 1, confirming a single valid charge.
The buyer's concern is likely a misunderstanding or a temporary bank hold.
No refund is warranted as the merchant is not at fault for a non-existent duplicate.
